clue.text: Send on message giving security code

parts.note: to pass something is to send it on to the next person
a word is a brief message, as in 'send word'

explanation.surface: Forwarding a message that contains a code for keeping things secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret term typed to gain access is a security code, the everyday login sense.

clue.text: Russian perhaps, half savage, swallowing litres

indicators.note: swallowing means the half-word takes the litre abbreviation inside itself
half of the word savage means only its first three letters are used

explanation.surface: A fierce Russian downing a lot of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half savage' gives SAV, and 'swallowing' puts L (litres) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians belong to the Slavic peoples of eastern Europe, so a Russian is one example; 'perhaps' flags it.

clue.text: Lament loss of second vessel

parts.note: MO is short for moment, as in 'wait a mo', so a second
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Grieving over a boat lost for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second vessel' reads as a ship, but 'second' is MO (a moment) and the vessel is an URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve for someone or something gone is to lament a loss.

clue.text: Surely he isn't this, for the bride?

definitions.text: Surely he isn't this, for the bride?

parts.words: Surely he isn't this, for the bride?
parts.note: the bride should think her groom is the finest man there, yet the title of finest goes to the groom's supporter

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a wedding guest is really the ideal man for the bride.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief attendant at a wedding carries this title, a pun on him not being the superior suitor.

clue.text: Earnings not safely secured

parts.note: reads as pay at financial risk, but means extra pay earned by doing unsafe work

explanation.surface: Wages that may not be paid, invested riskily.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra wages given for hazardous work are earned in peril, i.e. gained without safety.

clue.text: Turning to dry fish

indicators.note: turning means the words to and the champagne term are read backwards

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: Flipping a fish over so it can be dried.
explanation.definitionFit: A large European flatfish prized for eating is one species of fish.

clue.text: One putting up barrier for sportsman

definitions.meaning: a competitor in the sport of fencing, with foil, épée or sabre

explanation.surface: A man building a fence, described as an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a fence-builder, and also a swordsman competing in fencing.

clue.text: Programmed to avoid dirty thoughts?

parts.note: a mind indoctrinated is jokingly pictured as a mind scrubbed clean

explanation.surface: Someone conditioned never to think anything smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoctrinated means programmed; literally a laundered mind holds no dirty thoughts.

clue.text: Manage to find some cricket, and watch

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
to see is to watch

explanation.surface: Organising a trip to see some cricket and watch the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct work is to manage it.

clue.text: Family man, starting up new company, lives easily

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A family man launching a new business and living comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes the initials of 'up new company lives easily'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a male relative, so a family man in the literal kinship sense.

clue.text: Observe school's back

indicators.note: back means the school name is read in reverse

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Take note that term has started again.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON, the English boarding school, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice or remark something is to observe it.

clue.text: Battle later lost in court

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for courting

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters of later have gone astray and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A battle lost in a later court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' turns LATER into ATERL, placed 'in' WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington defeated Napoleon at this 1815 engagement in Belgium, so it names a famous battle.

clue.text: Cat turned up with mother

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is flipped round

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A cat that has come home with its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar or mountain lion of the Americas is a large wild cat.

clue.text: Show horror as daughter rushed madly round

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the daughter abbreviation
madly means the letters of rushed are rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: A parent recoiling as their daughter dashes about frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges RUSHED to SHUDER, which goes 'round' D.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble convulsively from fear or revulsion is to show horror.

clue.text: Successfully go the distance

parts.note: a boxer who lasts all the rounds and gets the judges' verdict triumphs this way

explanation.surface: Completing a long race or contest with success.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a fighter who survives every round and is ahead on the judges' scores takes the decision.

clue.text: Set of matches, and part of pencil, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a series of games, as in bridge or tennis, decided by the majority
an eraser, often fitted to a pencil's end

explanation.surface: A box of matches and a bit of a pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like things for lighting fires; it means games.
explanation.definitionFit: A best-of-three series in bridge or cricket, and also an eraser on a pencil.

clue.text: Fruit: millions found in Spanish city

indicators.note: found in means the millions letter is placed inside the city name

parts.note: León is a city in north-west Spain
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Fruit worth millions discovered in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour yellow citrus is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Reach from winding drive any part of chateau

indicators.note: winding means the letters of drive any twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting to the vineyard estate up the winding driveway of a French chateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges DRIVE ANY. 'Reach from' only links; a French wine chateau typically owns its vine plantation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine-making chateaux in Bordeaux include the land planted with grapevines as part of the estate.

clue.text: Adder's nest in this pavilion?

parts.note: an adder is one who adds up, i.e. a summer
a nest is a home, a house

explanation.surface: Finding a snake's nest inside a garden building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' looks like the snake; read it as one who adds, a SUMMER, whose nest is a HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light garden shelter used in warm weather is a small pavilion.

clue.text: Obstinate objections raised, and almost carried

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the objections word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: borne means carried

explanation.surface: Stubborn objections were raised and nearly won the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses BUTS to STUB; 'almost' cuts BORNE to BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unyieldingly set in their views is obstinate.

clue.text: With this, will you change later?

definitions.text: With this, will you change later?

parts.words: With this, will you change later?
parts.note: will is a testament, and this document amends it after it was drawn up

explanation.surface: Asking whether you will alter your plans afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' reads as the verb; it is the legal testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement added to a testament to alter it is the legal device meant.

clue.text: Film-maker became ratty, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film director who got irritable at times.
explanation.definitionFit: The device that records moving images literally makes the film, a witty twist on director.

clue.text: Expert died, buried in treacherous peat

indicators.note: buried in puts the died abbreviation inside the jumbled letters
treacherous means the letters of peat are untrustworthy and rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist died and was buried in dangerous bogland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treacherous' rearranges PEAT to AEPT; D goes 'buried in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled person is an expert in their field.

clue.text: Woman's love for brave man

parts.note: her is the possessive of a woman
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A woman's affection for a courageous man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man admired for courage is a hero.
